evidence.title: John Hunter, UC Davis Introduction to Analysis, chapter4
evidence.finding: Absolute convergence of a double series ensures both iterated sums exist and equal the unordered sum; checking an iterated sum of absolute values suffices through Tonelli/Fubini.
Tonelli applied to |a_ij| makes finite iterated absolute sum equal the product sum; Fubini then permits interchanging the signed/complex sums.

The direct signed-sum equality is usually called Fubini or Fubini-Tonelli; the answer uses Tonelli as shorthand for the combined argument. Lack of absolute convergence can, but need not, change the sum.
